claims.text: The starting nanoparticles are crystalline, near-equiatomic solid solutions composed of five or more metals.
Introducing a minor alloying element with a high negative enthalpy of mixing can stabilize the nanoparticles at 773–1173 K.
The minor alloying element reduces the nanoparticles' tendency toward phase separation.
The minor alloying element promotes a more homogeneous distribution of constituent elements.
Reduced phase separation and increased elemental homogeneity preserve nanoparticle structural stability.
Reduced phase separation and increased elemental homogeneity preserve nanoparticle chemical stability.
Alloyed nanoparticles will be more stable than otherwise identical nanoparticles without the minor alloying element.
Alloyed nanoparticles will exhibit better catalytic performance than nanoparticles without the minor alloying element.
The proposed stabilization is applicable over 773–1173 K and thermal exposures lasting several hours.
The effectiveness of stabilization depends on the identity and concentration of the minor alloying element and on the detailed nanoparticle composition and structure.
